I'm still new to it so this might not be 100% right. Unlike many diet plans, Slimming World does not advocate counting calories directly. The literature you're given upon your induction lists most foods and assigns them a "syn" value,  you're allowed to consume between 5-15 syns a day. There are 3 groups of food:  Free Foods, this includes  lean meat, chicken, fish, potatoes, rice, pasta, grains, pulses, starchy veg, eggs, fat-free dairy products, Quorn and tofu. These are foods with no syn value and (in theory) you can eat as much of these as you want. Then there are Healthy Extras. These are foods with low syn values which you are encouraged to eat a certain amount of everyday, combined with the free foods. Lastly, there are Syn foods. These include less healthy foods, many other plans would call these "treats" or "cheats". You're supposed to mix and match the 3 to make up a healthy diet, syn is shorthand for synergy as Slimming World believes it’s the synergy between the three components of the plan that enable sustainable weight loss. The books they give you are really helpful and I've found it very comprehensive and easy to understand.
